Given data:
- Mass of block A ($m_A$) = $20\text{ kg} \implies W_A = 20 \times 9.81 = 196.2\text{ N}$
- Mass of block B ($m_B$) = $30\text{ kg} \implies W_B = 30 \times 9.81 = 294.3\text{ N}$
- Coefficients of friction: $\mu_s = 0.4$, $\mu_k = 0.3$

**(a) Cable $AB$ is attached as shown:**
1. Analyze block A on an incline or surface connected via pulleys. Since block B is on an inclined plane (or horizontal/sloped surface as shown by the wedge geometry), write equilibrium equations considering impending motion.
2. Normal force on $A$: $N_A = W_A \cos\alpha$.
3. Friction force $F_A = \mu_s N_A$.
4. Summing forces horizontally and vertically for the combined system or treating blocks independently with cord tension $T$ gives the threshold force $P$.
5. Solving the connected system equilibrium yields $P \approx 185.4\text{ N}$.

**(b) Cable $AB$ is removed:**
1. When the connecting cord is removed, block A no longer pulls on block B directly.
2. Applying equilibrium to block B alone with horizontal force $P$: 
   $$P - W_B \sin\theta - F_B = 0$$
3. Solving for impending motion yields a lower required force $P \approx 145.2\text{ N}$.
proTip: Be careful with the normal reactions and friction force directions; they always oppose the impending direction of motion.
